# Hadronic Simplification

## Question

I am attaching the exact current NLO UU process card used by FACET. Please review the hadronic-variable reduction and simplification strategy as a perturbative-QCD/amplitudes theorist.

The package interprets the four entries in each Coordinates value in the null/transverse basis {nb,n,xhat,yhat}, with nb.n=1 and xhat^2=yhat^2=-1. It now infers, from the existing PartonMomentum, HadronMomentum, and MomentumFraction declarations,

ka = xa Pa,   kb = xb Pb,   kc = Ph/zh,

and substitutes the resulting direct coordinates together with the attached hadronic coordinates. Exact checks give ka.kb=s/2, ka.kc=-t/2, kb.kc=-u/2 and all mass, null-basis, and spin-orthogonality identities. No eta, PhT, S, T, or U is retained.

The immediate task is to choose where exact symbolic simplification should occur in a reverse-unitarity calculation:

1. each amplitude-conjugate pair coefficient before equal GLI targets are added;
2. each summed pre-IBP target coefficient;
3. each coefficient of a Kira master after reduction;
4. both 2 and 3.

The final hard coefficient must have only a common, trivial xa, xb, zh monomial together with the expected PDFs/FF, while its remaining coefficient is a function of s,t,u, epsilon, color, coupling, and (for TT) physical azimuthal structures. Give concrete advice about the algebraic ordering, especially whether kinematic substitution should occur before or after summing targets and whether one should simplify individual additive terms or the complete coefficient. Identify any branch-sensitive square-root issue in the attached direct coordinates and give an exact check that prevents a false cancellation. Do not propose fixed-point numerical evaluation as the calculation method.

## Pro response

Recommendation

Use option 4: simplify both the summed pre-IBP target coefficients and the final Kira-master coefficients.

Do not run a general Simplify or FullSimplify separately on every amplitude–conjugate pair. At the pair level, perform only exact kinematic reduction, branch-certified radical normalization, and inexpensive rational cleanup. The two important complete sums are

Later: explicit radical realization

The explicit square-root coordinates should be inserted into scalar coefficients only after all contributions to the same canonical GLI target have been added, unless a coefficient requires them earlier to remove residual hadronic vectors.

The best separation is therefore:

Pair-local: covariant hadron-to-parton relations and scalar-product reduction.

Target-level: direct-coordinate realization and branch-safe radical reduction.

Master-level: a second exact normalization after Kira accumulation.

If the implementation currently inserts the full components pair by pair, that remains algebraically valid, but it should not then run a costly general simplification on each pair. Preserve the resulting radicals as exact algebraic atoms until equal targets have been summed.

Exact branch certificate

A minimal Wolfram Language certificate is:

Wolfram Language
physicalAssumptions =
  s > 0 && t < 0 && u < 0 && s + t + u > 0 &&
  0 < xa < 1 && 0 < xb < 1 && 0 < zh < 1 &&
  Element[
    {s, t, u, xa, xb, zh, ST, STh, \[Phi]a, \[Phi]h},
    Reals
  ];

radicands = {
  s/(2 xa xb),
  xb/(2 s xa),
  xa/(2 s xb),
  t u/s,
  2 xa xb t u
};

branchCertificate = And[
  And @@ (
    TrueQ @ FullSimplify[
      # > 0,
      Assumptions -> physicalAssumptions
    ] & /@ radicands
  ),

  TrueQ @ FullSimplify[
    xb t + xa u < 0,
    Assumptions -> physicalAssumptions
  ],

  TrueQ @ FullSimplify[
    Sqrt[s/(2 xa xb)] Sqrt[xb/(2 s xa)] == 1/(2 xa),
    Assumptions -> physicalAssumptions
  ],

  TrueQ @ FullSimplify[
    Sqrt[s/(2 xa xb)] Sqrt[xa/(2 s xb)] == 1/(2 xb),
    Assumptions -> physicalAssumptions
  ],

  TrueQ @ FullSimplify[
    Sqrt[(xb t + xa u)^2] == -(xb t + xa u),
    Assumptions -> physicalAssumptions
  ],

  TrueQ @ FullSimplify[
    Sqrt[t] Sqrt[u]/Sqrt[s] == -Sqrt[t u/s],
    Assumptions -> physicalAssumptions
  ]
];

If[! TrueQ[branchCertificate],
  Message[HadronicReduction::branch];
  Return[$Failed]
];

Every manually introduced radical rewrite should additionally satisfy

Wolfram Language
certifiedRuleQ[lhs_ -> rhs_] :=
  TrueQ @ FullSimplify[
    lhs == rhs,
    Assumptions -> physicalAssumptions
  ];

PowerExpand should never be used in this path.
